lines.text: The little desk is still pretending it belongs in a loading dock. / A child-sized school desk has been dragged against the wall and promoted to dispatch.
All right. What were you in the middle of.

choices.text: run a thumb over the clean rectangle

lines.text: Dust everywhere except one clipboard-shaped patch. Whoever lifted it did so recently enough to leave the room two colours.
Took the paper. Left the desk. So—
Cable ties, a dead marker, two boiled sweets fused to their wrappers.
That is a night shift drawer if ever I saw one.
One tie has been cut cleanly. The thing it held is gone.
The drawer catches, then gives. Empty, except for a pencil worn flat on one side.
Somebody sat here long enough to make a pencil choose a side.
The same pages. The same last line waiting at the bottom. / Two sets of paper share one clip: your job on top, somebody else’s leaving underneath.
Mine says what to keep. Theirs says what to take away.
Crates. Lamps. Cable. Small things first, each crossed through in a quick dark stroke.
The strokes stop halfway down. Not messily. Simply stop.
Tea break, fire alarm, end of shift. Pick a boring reason.
The first half leans forward. By the last few lines the letters stand upright and press hard into the sheet.
Same hand. Less hurry. More frightened.
No. More careful. Those are not the same thing.
CHANDELIER — FRAME AND LOCK. No tick. No initials. Nothing written beneath it.
The page has been dented there by a pencil that never made a mark.
The hand reached this line and stopped.
Three place names remain. The people do not. / Magnets make a route down the board: DOCK. WEST STAIR. B3. Beside them, a row has been wiped almost clean.

choices.text: trace the route with a finger
tilt the board into the light

lines.text: Dock to stair to B3. Inward, downward. It is not a way out.
It is a handover. You walk the next person to the room that matters.
Then you come back up. Presumably.
The eraser left pale ghosts: four names, maybe five. One was rubbed until the board went dull.
Your reflection occupies the empty row.
Why take the names and leave the route.
The loose magnet is warm from your hand. Under it: RETURN.
There is no matching magnet for OUT.
The little work lamp remains exactly as dead as you left it. / A work lamp squats on the floor with its back hanging open.
You look useful. That is usually when the trouble starts.

choices.text: put a finger in the empty battery bay

lines.text: Click. A good, ordinary click. Nothing follows it.
Thank you. One honest thing in the room.
Cold contacts. Dust in the corners. The battery has been gone long enough for the empty space to have its own dirt.
Not flat. Not broken. Made unable.
The dead glass takes in the chandelier and gives you a tiny curved room.
For a moment there is room in that reflection for someone to stand behind the frame.
Enough.
The cart is still strapped upright, waiting to be useful. / A hand truck has been tied to the wall as if it might wander off.

choices.text: rub at the chalk on the foot

lines.text: Tight. Properly buckled, tail tucked away. Nobody dropped this and ran.
Somebody stopped work and still put their hands in order.
FRAME FIRST. The words blur under your thumb but do not come off.
Frame first. Then the thing inside it. Or keep the frame between you and the thing.
The wheel rolls half a turn and settles with the same crack in the rubber facing up.
Never carried the load. It was parked before the job began.
The stacked crates keep their neat little absences. / Three empty freight crates nest together, all corners and old tape.
Everything gets a box. Even things nobody intends to keep.
GLASS. CABLE. LENSES. Each word appears on several generations of tape.
This room has packed itself up more than once.
The cloth smells of rain and hot dust. Something round left a clean bowl in it.
A lamp, probably.
Too large for the work lamp. Too small for the chandelier.
No long case. No padded crate. Nothing here could take the chandelier without breaking it down.
So the frame is the box.
Then why lock the box from the outside.
The open case waits with the patience of an empty mouth. / A black road case lies open near the wall. The foam inside was cut around a recorder almost the size of yours.
I know your voice now. Short. Dry. Close. / Previous recordist, then. Or somebody with the same expensive habits.

choices.text: fit your hand into the empty shape

lines.text: Your recorder would fit if you worried the corners. The missing one was broader, older, carried by both hands.
He put it down here and took the machine with him.
Or the machine went and left the case.
No name. One strip of peeled tape and, under the handle, four tally marks cut with a key.
There is space for a fifth.
Four of something.
The latch cracks shut. The case answers with one small metal cough.
There. Now I know where that sound lives.
The reel has not grown a cable while your back was turned. / A cable reel stands by the salvage rack. No cable. Just the wheel and a handle polished by hands.
Hollow thing. You carry a sound better than a cable. / Empty, but not abandoned. Somebody wound it clean.
One click under your palm. Then the empty wheel rings longer than it ought to.
Easy. It is a big hollow thing in a bigger hollow thing.
Through the hub you can see the chandelier, reduced to a bright little cage.
As you move, the bars slide across it like a shutter.
There is no loose end. The drum is clean.
The room offers several coils. None reach it.
So where is the cable that fed the chandelier.
The long steel bar waits in its clips along the shutter. / A steel bar runs shoulder-high across the loading shutter. Put a knuckle to it and the whole wall rings.
I felt that one in my teeth. / That will travel.

choices.text: put an ear to the steel

lines.text: The knock runs away through the shutter and returns from somewhere above you.
That is the roof coming back. Has to be.
The chandelier trembles once.
Cold paint against your cheek. Beyond it: rain, a road far off, and something ticking too slowly to be water.
The ticking stops when you name it.
A black line of yard. One weed laid flat by the weather. No feet on the other side.
Good. Obviously.
The chandelier waits inside its frame, too low for a ceiling and too carefully held for rubbish. / A chandelier hangs at eye level inside a wheeled cage. Each arm is wrapped. Every wheel is locked.
You are the only thing in here being treated like it might wake up.

choices.text: compare it with the unfinished list
look at it through the dead lamp

lines.text: You lean your weight into the frame. Rubber complains against concrete. The wheels do not turn.
Not parked. Fixed.
The locks face outward, where a person could reach them. Nothing inside could.
A cloth-wrapped lead runs down the stem and ends above the floor, neatly cut and tied back.
No plug. No hidden run. Nothing reaches a wall.
FRAME AND LOCK. Beneath it, in softer pencil: DO NOT HANG.
Nobody was going to put you back up.
The tag is dated for tomorrow.
The words match: CHANDELIER — FRAME AND LOCK.
This is where their job stopped.
And where mine starts. That is cheerful.
In the dead lamp’s curved glass, the frame closes into a little room behind you.
Empty.
Stop checking.
The work lamp is still dead. It is beginning to feel stubborn about it. / You crouch beside the work lamp because it is the only light in the room that behaved.

choices.text: look for the figure in its glass

lines.text: Click. Nothing.
Good.
Why is that good.
The battery space is empty. It was empty before. Your fingertip comes away grey with the same old dust.
One light had no power. The other had no excuse.
Only your eye, bent wide in the curved glass.
I saw it here first. Or I saw enough to become afraid of the rest.
The case has not returned to where you remember it. / The road case sits a little farther from the wall. Not much. Enough that you have to choose whether you know.
The latch came from across the room. This stayed here. I watched it stay here. / I never touched this one. I do not get to pretend I know where it was.

choices.text: look at the four tally marks
put it back against the wall

lines.text: Closed now. The bright edge sits under your thumb exactly where it did before.
One sound. Two places.
Closed now. You cannot remember whether it was open.
That is what I get for not touching things the first time.
Four cuts under the handle. Space for a fifth.
He came back here four times.
Or something wanted the next person to think he did.
You slide it back. It leaves a clean track through fresh dust.
Fresh.
Do not say that like it helps.
The handle rests one tooth past certainty. / The reel handle is not where you left it. Or it is precisely where you left it and the room has moved around the memory.
I heard you behind the desk. You were in front of me. / I did not turn you. I am nearly sure I did not turn you.

choices.text: mark the tooth with a pencil

lines.text: A pencil line across metal and frame. Crude. Undeniable.
There. Move now.
It does not.
Your palm cups the handle. The wheel is cold and still.
Behind the dispatch desk, something gives one soft click.
Through the hub: broken bulbs, black arms, no figure.
I liked it better when this was a trick of perspective.
The steel is quiet now. Too thoroughly quiet. / The shutter bar hums so faintly you feel it before you hear it.
My knock came back from above the chandelier. There is no steel between here and there. / I never knocked this. Whatever is in it belongs to the room.

choices.text: stop the hum with your hand

lines.text: The hum stops under your palm.
Something in the chandelier frame stops at the same instant.
I am not doing call and response with a room.
Rain. The far road. The weed still pressed flat.
Outside is exactly where I left it.
You do not open the shutter to make sure.
Your knuckle lands. The bar takes the sound away.
It does not return.
Worse.
The frame still holds the shape of what happened. / The bulbs are black mouths now. Glass lies inside the cage in a neat bright weather.
Start with what stayed put.
One, two, three, four. Locked. You shove until the cage complains and your shoulder hurts.
It never moved.
Neither did I, for a while.
Still tied back. Still ending in open air.
No wire. No battery. No somebody at a switch.
The simple explanations leave in that order.
Behind the frame: bare wall, two scuffs, your own shadow.
One of us was here.
The glass is warm.
Of course it is. It just—
No. It was dark long enough. It should be cold.
